analysis:
At COP26 on 1 November 2021, PM Narendra Modi stated India would take its non-fossil energy capacity to 500 GW by 2030.

MNRE data show total non-fossil installed capacity of 308.03 GW as on 30 September 2026. PIB reported India crossed 300 GW of non-fossil capacity as on 31 July 2026, about 60% of the 500 GW target. CEA data put non-fossil sources at 54.18% of 548.86 GW installed capacity as on 30 June 2026.

The target year is 2030, so the commitment is still open and is recorded as in progress.
notes: The COP26 speech was delivered on 1 November 2021; the MEA transcript page is dated 2 November 2021, so the date field uses the speech date and this is flagged. The English wording follows the PMO/MEA official translation and is therefore not marked verbatim. The separate COP26 '50% of energy requirements from renewables by 2030' pledge was not used here to avoid overlap with bjp-joshi-2025-50pc-nonfossil-achieved (which concerns installed capacity, not generation).
